title: Rectangular base
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, draw a two-dimensional sketch consisting of a closed loop made up of four lines. The first line starts at the origin and ends at coordinates (0.0117, 0.0). The second line extends from this point to (0.0117, 0.0194). The third line then moves to (0.0, 0.0194), and the fourth line completes the loop back to the origin. Apply a scale factor of 0.0194 to the entire sketch to adjust its size proportionally. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object using the same Euler angles and translation vector. Next, extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular base are 0.011728395061728396 meters in length, 0.019444444444444445 meters in width, and 0.75 meters in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the rectangular protrusion
sketch = (
    workplane
    .lineTo(0.0117, 0.0)  # line_1
    .lineTo(0.0117, 0.0194)  # line_2
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0194)  # line_3
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0)  # line_4
    .close()  # Close the loop
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the rectangular protrusion
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# The final model 'r' is the extruded shape
r = extrusion

# Display the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0117, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0117, 0.0194) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0194) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular section
r = r.extrude(0.75)
